pathway.title: Range Resources Corp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage is low and falling, so debt service is not the binding constraint today. Total debt at carrying value fell from USD 1,697.88 million at FY2024 to USD 780.92 million at 2026-09-30, while derived EBITDA rose from USD 727.72 million to USD 1,593.77 million over the last twelve months, so total debt over EBITDA moved from 2.33x to 0.92x at FY2025 and 0.49x now, and EBITDA covered cash interest paid 20.33x. Adding the divestiture contract obligation and operating leases, which sit outside reported debt and total USD 378.82 million, gives USD 1,159.74 million and 0.73x. The fall came from repaying the 2025 notes at maturity and redeeming the 2029 notes with cash flow and revolver borrowings, so the remaining debt is one floating-rate bank facility and one fixed-rate note. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 107–108; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3, 8, 16; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-03; calculation C-04; calculation C-05; calculation C-07; calculation C-08; calculation C-10; calculation C-09

Refinancing risk is remote before 2030 and liquidity is adequate, but it rests on one bank facility. The revolver and the 4.75% senior notes both fall due in 2030 and total USD 794.00 million of principal, or 0.50x LTM EBITDA; the revolver has commitments of USD 2,000.00 million, of which USD 294.00 million is drawn and USD 165.10 million is committed to letters of credit, leaving USD 1,540.90 million undrawn against USD 1,716.80 million at FY2025, while cash was only USD 12 thousand. The borrowing base of USD 3,000.00 million is above the commitments and lenders left it unchanged at FY2024, FY2025 and 2026-09-30, even though the present value of proved reserves discounted at 10% was USD 5,454 million at FY2024 and USD 11,566 million at FY2025. A rise of 1 percentage point in the floating rate would cost USD 2.94 million a year on the drawn revolver, which is immaterial. The fair value of the notes due 2030 was 95.03% of principal at 2026-09-30, down 3.75 percentage points from 98.78% at FY2025 and above the 93.86% at FY2024; the filing gives no cause. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9, 12, 34; 10-K_2024-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 91, 133; calculation C-55; calculation C-11; calculation C-56; calculation C-46; calculation C-47; calculation C-48; calculation C-49

Revenue is price-driven and only partly hedged, so earnings will swing with gas prices. In 9M 2026 product sales grew 18.37% on realized prices before derivative settlements up 11.95% and production up 5.74%, but in Q3 2026 the realized natural gas price before settlements fell 7.03% year on year to USD 2.38 per mcf while production rose 12.18%, so the growth came from volume, NGLs and oil. Natural gas, NGLs and oil were 57.78%, 36.45% and 5.78% of 9M 2026 product sales. Gas derivatives cover 36.28% of Q3 2026 gas production for Q4 2026, 20.59% for 2027 and 11.76% for 2028, and management says more than 30% of projected production for the remainder of 2026 is hedged; the three-way collars give no protection below their sold put prices. Only one customer reached 10% of FY2025 sales, and purchasers are readily replaced, so customer concentration is not a credit concern. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 20–21, 23–24, 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 122; calculation C-24; calculation C-26; calculation C-25; calculation C-27; calculation C-29; calculation C-30; calculation C-31; calculation C-32; calculation C-33

Margins are strong but the cost base is rigid at the transport and processing line. The LTM EBITDA margin was 45.14% against 30.11% at FY2024, when revenue fell 28.38%; transportation, gathering, processing and compression was 54.86% of 9M 2026 costs and expenses, at USD 1.55 per mcfe against USD 1.51 per mcfe in 9M 2025, and minimum commitments were USD 5,857.88 million at FY2025. The smallest annual minimum payment for 2026 to 2028 is 10.28x LTM cash interest paid, so the claim ahead of equity that the cost base represents is far larger than debt service. These commitments rose by about USD 1,500 million in 9M 2026 when new pipeline and processing capacity started, and management attributes part of the higher unit cost to processing charges that rise with commodity prices, which softens the rigidity only partly. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 92, 108; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 17, 21–22; calculation C-19; calculation C-20; calculation C-22; calculation C-34; calculation C-35; calculation C-36

Cash conversion is good and capital spending is the flexible lever. LTM operating cash flow of USD 1,419.26 million was 0.89x EBITDA and capital expenditure of USD 692.07 million, including acreage, took 48.76% of it, leaving USD 727.19 million of free cash flow, or 0.46x EBITDA. The 2026 capital budget is USD 650 million to USD 700 million and management reviews it through the year against prices. Reported EBITDA for 9M 2026 includes USD 60.38 million of derivative income that was not cash, or 4.88% of EBITDA, and cash income taxes paid were only USD 11.08 million, or 1.22% of pre-tax income, because federal net operating losses of USD 1,100 million at FY2025 shelter income; 94.21% of the 9M 2026 tax expense was deferred. Conversion will weaken as those losses are used, and the estimated future development cost of proved undeveloped reserves is USD 1,800 million. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 93, 127, 151; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 16, 33; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-12; calculation C-13; calculation C-14; calculation C-16; calculation C-15; calculation C-17; calculation C-37; calculation C-38; calculation C-39; calculation C-40; calculation C-41

Financial policy has been creditor-aligned so far, but the EQT merger moves the capital structure beyond what the filings describe. Shareholder returns in 9M 2026 were USD 176.31 million, or 28.24% of free cash flow, and no sponsor extraction is documented. The remaining repurchase authorization of USD 1,421.65 million is 1.79x debt principal, so a debt-funded acceleration is possible and its limit is not known without the credit agreement. The all-stock merger would leave Range shareholders with about 27% and EQT shareholders with about 73% of the combined company, with closing expected in Q1 2027; the filings do not say whether Range's debt stays in place, is refinanced or is guaranteed, or whether the 101% repurchase right on the notes applies. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 8, 18–19, 46, 49; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-52; calculation C-53; calculation C-54

Asset value covers debt many times at reserve-report prices, which supports loss severity more than it protects against refinancing stress. The reserve present value was 9.50x debt principal of USD 1,218.00 million at FY2025, and 3.19x the principal of USD 1,708.70 million at FY2024, when the benchmark gas price used was 37.17% lower and the reserve present value was 52.84% lower. That value is a management measure at regulatory pricing that excludes derivatives and income taxes, so it is an indicator, not a recovery estimate. The revolver is secured by substantially all assets, while the filings do not state whether the notes are secured or how they rank against the bank debt, so who benefits from this coverage is not established. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 129, 131, 155; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; calculation C-42; calculation C-43; calculation C-44; calculation C-45

runs.text: The first strength is low leverage with high cover: total debt of USD 780.92 million against LTM EBITDA of USD 1,593.77 million gives 0.49x and cash interest cover of 20.33x, which leaves room to absorb a price fall, repay the revolver and keep the 2030 maturities refinanceable. The second is a long, undrawn funding runway: USD 1,540.90 million is undrawn on a revolver that matures in 2030, and the borrowing base of USD 3,000.00 million is above the commitments, so liquidity does not depend on market access. The third is a deep, low-reinvestment-risk asset base, with reserve life of 22.23 years and 71% of proved reserves developed, so cash flow can be sustained within the capital budget and the reserve present value of USD 11,566 million at FY2025 is 9.50x principal. The fourth is discretionary capital spending and creditor-aligned distributions: LTM free cash flow of USD 727.19 million is 0.46x EBITDA, 9M 2026 shareholder returns were 28.24% of free cash flow, and there is no sponsor. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 8–9, 34; 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-03; calculation C-07; calculation C-11; calculation C-14; calculation C-53; calculation C-42; calculation C-71

The first weakness is single-basin gas price exposure: substantially all output comes from the Marcellus Shale, 64% of proved reserves are natural gas, and gas derivatives cover only 20.59% of Q3 2026 production for 2027, so a gas price fall reaches cash flow quickly. The second is fixed transport and processing cost: minimum commitments of USD 5,857.88 million at FY2025 rose by about USD 1,500 million in 9M 2026, and each year's minimum is at least 10.28x LTM cash interest, so margins fall faster than revenue. The third is dependence on the bank facility with almost no cash, so a borrowing base cut or a covenant problem would reach liquidity directly, while covenant headroom cannot be calculated. The fourth is the open merger: control of the capital structure would pass to a group in which Range holders would own about 27%, and creditor treatment, the revolver and the notes' repurchase right are not stated. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 92; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 9–11, 17–19, 38; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-32; calculation C-35; calculation C-36

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The only transaction of scale is the EQT merger. On 2026-10-25 Range entered into an agreement to combine with EQT Corporation in an all-stock merger at a fixed exchange ratio, after which EQT shareholders would own about 73% and Range shareholders about 27% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis. Both boards approved the merger unanimously; it needs the approval of each company's shareholders, expiry or termination of the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period, effectiveness of EQT's registration statement and New York Stock Exchange listing of the new shares, and it is expected to close in Q1 2027. Either party may terminate if the merger has not closed within 12 months of the agreement, extended automatically to 18 months if only antitrust or legal-restraint conditions remain. In specified terminations Range would pay EQT USD 423 million and EQT would pay Range USD 1,148 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19, 42, 46

The filings supplied describe no new senior notes. The exhibit index in the annual report lists no indenture after the one dated February 2022 for the 4.75% senior notes due 2030. The new debt arrangements are the amended and restated revolving credit facility entered into in October 2025, which extends maturity to 2030-10-02, raises commitments from USD 1,500 million to USD 2,000 million and keeps a borrowing base of USD 3,000 million, and the January 2026 redemption of the 8.25% senior notes due 2029 at 101.375% of par using revolver borrowings. The filings state no cash consideration, debt assumption or refinancing in the merger. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 131, 155; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 18, 34

fields.value: Range's reported leverage is low and falling: carrying-value debt was 0.49x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 2026-09-30, against 2.33x at FY2024, so creditors face little balance-sheet leverage on the filings' own figures. That view rests on EBITDA derived in this analysis, because the issuer reports none, and it excludes USD 241.48 million of divestiture obligations; adding them and operating leases gives 0.73x.

fields.value: Carrying-value debt fell from USD 1,697.88 million at FY2024 to USD 1,198.33 million at FY2025 and USD 780.92 million at 2026-09-30, while derived EBITDA rose from USD 727.72 million to USD 1,307.05 million for FY2025 and USD 1,593.77 million over the last twelve months, so total debt over EBITDA moved from 2.33x to 0.92x to 0.49x. The FY2025 fall followed the repayment of the notes due 2025 at maturity from cash on hand and revolver borrowings, with revenue up 28.90%. In 9M 2026 the 8.25% notes due 2029 were redeemed using revolver borrowings, which rose by a net USD 176.00 million over the nine months, while operating cash flow of USD 1,161.75 million funded capital spending and shareholder returns. For creditors this means leverage is now set by shareholder-return and merger decisions rather than by operating strain.

fields.value: Cash was only USD 12 thousand at 2026-09-30 and USD 204 thousand at FY2025, so liquidity is the undrawn revolver: commitments of USD 2,000.00 million less USD 294.00 million drawn and USD 165.10 million of undrawn letters of credit leave USD 1,540.90 million, down from USD 1,716.80 million at FY2025 as net revolver borrowings rose by USD 176.00 million. The revolver is secured by substantially all assets, matures on 2030-10-02 and has a borrowing base of USD 3,000.00 million, above its commitments; the only other debt is USD 500.00 million of notes due 2030. Liquidity therefore depends on the lenders' continued commitments and compliance with covenants whose levels the interim reports do not print.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The merger agreement signed with EQT on 2026-10-25 is an all-stock transaction expected to close in Q1 2027. The quarterly report states no cash consideration, debt assumption or refinancing, so no pro forma net debt is stated and every figure here is before the merger. Termination fees of USD 423 million payable by Range and USD 1,148 million payable by EQT are contingent and are not adjustments to net debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against reading Range as lightly levered is that reported EBITDA includes USD 60.38 million of non-cash derivative gains in 9M 2026 and excludes USD 241.48 million of divestiture obligations and USD 137.34 million of operating leases; with the obligations added, leverage is 0.73x rather than 0.49x, which is still low. Shareholder returns of USD 176.31 million in 9M 2026 were 28.24% of free cash flow of USD 624.25 million, so they do not strain leverage today. The view would weaken if buybacks and dividends outran free cash flow and the revolver funded the gap, or if lower prices turned derivative gains into losses; the pending merger could change the capital structure in ways the filings do not state.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Range Resources Corp (issuer rrc-315852), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit_snapshot pathway (the full credit assessment). The scope is the issuer's business and operating model, ownership and control, governance and financial policy, issuer history and the pending EQT merger, drawn from the five supplied filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The supplied output of an earlier module of this run:

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Document dates are the signature dates printed in each filing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor and governance risk is medium on the evidence supplied: Range has no sponsor and no documented creditor-adverse action, but the all-stock EQT merger signed after quarter end leaves post-merger control and creditor treatment unstated, so creditors cannot yet price the surviving obligor. Distributions are modest against operating cash flow, and the filings supplied document no debt-funded recapitalisation or liability-management exercise.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is a single-basin gas producer: substantially all reserves and production are in the Marcellus Shale, reserves equal 22.23 years of FY2025 production, and fixed transportation and gathering commitments of USD 5,857.88 million at FY2025 year end exceed USD 794.00 million of debt principal at 2026-09-30, so volume and price shocks reach cash flow quickly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 81, 92; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C-01; calculation C-13; calculation C-07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Range has no sponsor or controlling shareholder in the supplied documents, so the extraction risk that dominates sponsor-owned credits is absent, but ownership percentages, the full board composition and independence, and related-party dealings are not established because the annual report takes them from a proxy statement that was not supplied. The company is a listed public company whose share count at 2026-10-23 equals shares issued less treasury shares at 2026-09-30, so the equity base is consistent across the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Documented financial policy is creditor-neutral to supportive. Shareholder returns in 9M 2026 were USD 105.48 million of buybacks and USD 70.83 million of dividends, USD 176.31 million together and 15.18% of operating cash flow of USD 1,161.75 million; in FY2025 they were USD 316.25 million, or 27.00% of operating cash flow of USD 1,171.32 million. The board raised the repurchase authorization to USD 1,500.00 million in February 2026 and USD 1,421.65 million remained at 2026-09-30, which is larger than the USD 794.00 million of debt principal outstanding, so a debt-funded acceleration is possible and the limit on it is not established because the credit agreement was not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 8, 35, 49; 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, page 109; calculation C-04; calculation C-05; calculation C-14; calculation C-15; calculation C-16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The EQT merger moves control of Range's capital structure to the combined company: Range shareholders would own about 27% and EQT shareholders about 73% on a fully diluted basis, each Range share converts at a fixed exchange ratio, closing is expected in Q1 2027, and until then the agreement restricts Range's corporate transactions without EQT's consent. For creditors the open points are that the filing does not say whether Range survives as a subsidiary, whether the change-of-control repurchase right at 101% of principal applies to the notes, or whether the revolver is refinanced. Termination fees of USD 423 million payable by Range and USD 1,148 million payable by EQT make a failed deal costly for Range.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Range is a concentrated producer with a large fixed cost base. Substantially all reserves and production are in the Marcellus Shale in Pennsylvania, product sales in 9M 2026 were 57.78% natural gas, 36.45% NGLs and 5.78% oil, and transportation, gathering, processing and compression was USD 990.08 million, or 54.86% of costs and expenses. Minimum transportation and gathering commitments of USD 5,857.88 million at FY2025 year end, which rose by about USD 1,500 million in 9M 2026, are a fixed element of that cost, so lower prices cannot be offset by cutting it quickly, and cash flow is sensitive to price and to the availability of third-party pipelines.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 57, 92; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 17, 23; calculation C-03; calculation C-09; calculation C-13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A legacy obligation sits outside the debt measures: the 2020 sale of the North Louisiana assets left gathering, transportation and processing contracts that give no future benefit, with a balance of USD 241.48 million at 2026-09-30 and obligations that extend into 2030. Natural gas hedges run through 2029 and basis swaps through 2030, with shorter NGLs and oil hedges, and stabilise some cash flow; the net derivative position is USD 126.22 million, but hedges cover only part of output and their fair value is not cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 16; calculation C-08; calculation C-11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure supports monitoring of public financial statements but not of lender terms. The auditor, in place since 2003, gave an unqualified opinion on the FY2025 statements and an opinion that internal control was effective, and management concluded that disclosure controls were effective at 2026-09-30; compliance with the credit agreement and notes is stated without figures, and compliance certificates, basket usage and the credit agreement are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a lower risk level is behavioural: Range has no sponsor, no documented amendment, waiver or liability-management exercise, a record of retiring notes below par or at maturity and of calling the 2029 notes at a small premium, and distributions that are small against operating cash flow. The level would fall to low if the merger documents show that Range's debt is assumed, refinanced or left in place on terms at least as protective as today's. It would rise to high if the merger agreement or credit agreement allows debt-funded distributions or leaves Range's creditors behind a more heavily indebted parent, or if buybacks outran free cash flow and the revolver funded them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so the full board composition, director independence, ownership percentages and related-party dealings are not established, which holds the control and alignment conclusion at medium rather than low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The merger agreement and EQT's filings are not supplied, so the post-merger obligor and creditor treatment rest on one note and the risk factors in the quarterly report, and the merger conclusion cannot go beyond what that report says.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so capacity for distributions, investments and further debt is not established, and the financial-policy conclusion rests on observed behaviour only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Reserve life and cost measures come from management's own figures; the independent reserve audit described in the annual report is not supplied, so the reserve-life conclusion rests on management's estimate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The only transaction of scale is the EQT merger. On 2026-10-25 Range entered into an agreement to combine with EQT Corporation in an all-stock merger at a fixed exchange ratio, after which EQT shareholders would own about 73% and Range shareholders about 27% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis. Both boards approved the merger unanimously; it needs the approval of each company's shareholders, expiry or termination of the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period, effectiveness of EQT's registration statement and New York Stock Exchange listing of the new shares, and it is expected to close in Q1 2027. Either party may terminate if the merger has not closed within 12 months of the agreement, extended automatically to 18 months if only antitrust or legal-restraint conditions remain. In specified terminations Range would pay EQT USD 423 million and EQT would pay Range USD 1,148 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The filings supplied describe no new senior notes. The exhibit index in the annual report lists no indenture after the one dated February 2022 for the 4.75% senior notes due 2030. The new debt arrangements are the amended and restated revolving credit facility entered into in October 2025, which extends maturity to 2030-10-02, raises commitments from USD 1,500 million to USD 2,000 million and keeps a borrowing base of USD 3,000 million, and the January 2026 redemption of the 8.25% senior notes due 2029 at 101.375% of par using revolver borrowings. The filings state no cash consideration, debt assumption or refinancing in the merger.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The level is driven by the pending merger and unknown legal capacity, because they leave the obligor and the limits on distributions unstated, which implies that creditor treatment cannot yet be priced. Countervailing evidence is the absence of a sponsor, distributions funded from operating cash flow and debt reduction in 2025 and 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Range Resources Corp (issuer rrc-315852), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit_snapshot pathway (the full credit assessment). The scope is the issuer's overall fundamental credit profile, its strongest support, its primary downside and the signals to monitor, built from the five supplied filings and the three earlier modules of this run. It is a stand-alone view: the effect of the pending EQT merger on creditors is not assessed because the filings do not state it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The supplied outputs of earlier modules of this run:

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Document dates are the signature dates printed in each filing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Range's fundamental credit profile is strong on leverage and liquidity and adequate on business risk, so creditors are well covered on current numbers, but dependence on gas prices, fixed transport costs and the unresolved EQT merger are the threats to watch. Total debt is 0.49x derived EBITDA for the last twelve months at 2026-09-30, EBITDA covers cash interest 20.33x, no debt matures before 2030 and the undrawn revolver gives USD 1,540.90 million of liquidity. The main downside is a gas price fall that cuts EBITDA while minimum transport payments stay due: a fall that returned EBITDA to its FY2024 level of USD 727.72 million would lift total debt to 1.07x EBITDA and turn free cash flow negative, but would not threaten liquidity or the 2030 maturities. Creditor treatment in the merger is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 8–9, 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, page 108; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-03; calculation C-07; calculation C-11; calculation C-58; calculation C-60; calculation C-65

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is low and falling, so debt service is not the binding constraint today. Total debt at carrying value fell from USD 1,697.88 million at FY2024 to USD 780.92 million at 2026-09-30, while derived EBITDA rose from USD 727.72 million to USD 1,593.77 million over the last twelve months, so total debt over EBITDA moved from 2.33x to 0.92x at FY2025 and 0.49x now, and EBITDA covered cash interest paid 20.33x. Adding the divestiture contract obligation and operating leases, which sit outside reported debt and total USD 378.82 million, gives USD 1,159.74 million and 0.73x. The fall came from repaying the 2025 notes at maturity and redeeming the 2029 notes with cash flow and revolver borrowings, so the remaining debt is one floating-rate bank facility and one fixed-rate note.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 107–108; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3, 8, 16; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-03; calculation C-04; calculation C-05; calculation C-07; calculation C-08; calculation C-10; calculation C-09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing risk is remote before 2030 and liquidity is adequate, but it rests on one bank facility. The revolver and the 4.75% senior notes both fall due in 2030 and total USD 794.00 million of principal, or 0.50x LTM EBITDA; the revolver has commitments of USD 2,000.00 million, of which USD 294.00 million is drawn and USD 165.10 million is committed to letters of credit, leaving USD 1,540.90 million undrawn against USD 1,716.80 million at FY2025, while cash was only USD 12 thousand. The borrowing base of USD 3,000.00 million is above the commitments and lenders left it unchanged at FY2024, FY2025 and 2026-09-30, even though the present value of proved reserves discounted at 10% was USD 5,454 million at FY2024 and USD 11,566 million at FY2025. A rise of 1 percentage point in the floating rate would cost USD 2.94 million a year on the drawn revolver, which is immaterial. The fair value of the notes due 2030 was 95.03% of principal at 2026-09-30, down 3.75 percentage points from 98.78% at FY2025 and above the 93.86% at FY2024; the filing gives no cause.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9, 12, 34; 10-K_2024-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 91, 133; calculation C-55; calculation C-11; calculation C-56; calculation C-46; calculation C-47; calculation C-48; calculation C-49

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is price-driven and only partly hedged, so earnings will swing with gas prices. In 9M 2026 product sales grew 18.37% on realized prices before derivative settlements up 11.95% and production up 5.74%, but in Q3 2026 the realized natural gas price before settlements fell 7.03% year on year to USD 2.38 per mcf while production rose 12.18%, so the growth came from volume, NGLs and oil. Natural gas, NGLs and oil were 57.78%, 36.45% and 5.78% of 9M 2026 product sales. Gas derivatives cover 36.28% of Q3 2026 gas production for Q4 2026, 20.59% for 2027 and 11.76% for 2028, and management says more than 30% of projected production for the remainder of 2026 is hedged; the three-way collars give no protection below their sold put prices. Only one customer reached 10% of FY2025 sales, and purchasers are readily replaced, so customer concentration is not a credit concern.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 20–21, 23–24, 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 122; calculation C-24; calculation C-26; calculation C-25; calculation C-27; calculation C-29; calculation C-30; calculation C-31; calculation C-32; calculation C-33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are strong but the cost base is rigid at the transport and processing line. The LTM EBITDA margin was 45.14% against 30.11% at FY2024, when revenue fell 28.38%; transportation, gathering, processing and compression was 54.86% of 9M 2026 costs and expenses, at USD 1.55 per mcfe against USD 1.51 per mcfe in 9M 2025, and minimum commitments were USD 5,857.88 million at FY2025. The smallest annual minimum payment for 2026 to 2028 is 10.28x LTM cash interest paid, so the claim ahead of equity that the cost base represents is far larger than debt service. These commitments rose by about USD 1,500 million in 9M 2026 when new pipeline and processing capacity started, and management attributes part of the higher unit cost to processing charges that rise with commodity prices, which softens the rigidity only partly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 92, 108; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 17, 21–22; calculation C-19; calculation C-20; calculation C-22; calculation C-34; calculation C-35; calculation C-36

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is good and capital spending is the flexible lever. LTM operating cash flow of USD 1,419.26 million was 0.89x EBITDA and capital expenditure of USD 692.07 million, including acreage, took 48.76% of it, leaving USD 727.19 million of free cash flow, or 0.46x EBITDA. The 2026 capital budget is USD 650 million to USD 700 million and management reviews it through the year against prices. Reported EBITDA for 9M 2026 includes USD 60.38 million of derivative income that was not cash, or 4.88% of EBITDA, and cash income taxes paid were only USD 11.08 million, or 1.22% of pre-tax income, because federal net operating losses of USD 1,100 million at FY2025 shelter income; 94.21% of the 9M 2026 tax expense was deferred. Conversion will weaken as those losses are used, and the estimated future development cost of proved undeveloped reserves is USD 1,800 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 93, 127, 151; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 16, 33; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-12; calculation C-13; calculation C-14; calculation C-16; calculation C-15; calculation C-17; calculation C-37; calculation C-38; calculation C-39; calculation C-40; calculation C-41

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy has been creditor-aligned so far, but the EQT merger moves the capital structure beyond what the filings describe. Shareholder returns in 9M 2026 were USD 176.31 million, or 28.24% of free cash flow, and no sponsor extraction is documented. The remaining repurchase authorization of USD 1,421.65 million is 1.79x debt principal, so a debt-funded acceleration is possible and its limit is not known without the credit agreement. The all-stock merger would leave Range shareholders with about 27% and EQT shareholders with about 73% of the combined company, with closing expected in Q1 2027; the filings do not say whether Range's debt stays in place, is refinanced or is guaranteed, or whether the 101% repurchase right on the notes applies.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 8, 18–19, 46, 49; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-52; calculation C-53; calculation C-54

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Asset value covers debt many times at reserve-report prices, which supports loss severity more than it protects against refinancing stress. The reserve present value was 9.50x debt principal of USD 1,218.00 million at FY2025, and 3.19x the principal of USD 1,708.70 million at FY2024, when the benchmark gas price used was 37.17% lower and the reserve present value was 52.84% lower. That value is a management measure at regulatory pricing that excludes derivatives and income taxes, so it is an indicator, not a recovery estimate. The revolver is secured by substantially all assets, while the filings do not state whether the notes are secured or how they rank against the bank debt, so who benefits from this coverage is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 129, 131, 155; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; calculation C-42; calculation C-43; calculation C-44; calculation C-45

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against the favourable view is that the leverage figures are flattered by a strong price year and ignore fixed claims. Derived EBITDA includes USD 60.38 million of non-cash derivative income, excludes USD 378.82 million of divestiture and lease claims that lift leverage to 0.73x, and sits ahead of minimum transport payments of at least 10.28x LTM cash interest each year. Cash was USD 12 thousand, so liquidity is the revolver alone, and the balance-sheet current ratio was 0.74x at 2026-09-30 and 0.67x at FY2025, against a covenant floor of 1.00x that is measured on the credit agreement's own definition and cannot be tested here. Natural gas is 64% of proved reserves, the realized gas price fell 7.03% year on year in Q3 2026, and the merger could place Range's creditors behind a more heavily indebted parent. The view would weaken if EBITDA fell toward the FY2024 level while buybacks continued, if the revolver funded returns or merger costs, if the borrowing base were cut below the commitments, or if the merger documents leave Range's creditors with less protection. It would strengthen if those documents show the debt assumed or guaranteed by a stronger obligor, and if the credit agreement shows wide covenant headroom.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3, 24, 38; 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, page 131; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C-37; calculation C-10; calculation C-35; calculation C-50; calculation C-51; calculation C-27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The downside conclusion rests on an arithmetic illustration with prices lowered and costs, volumes, hedges, working capital and taxes held unchanged, so it shows the order of magnitude of the damage and not a forecast, and a real price fall would be partly offset by hedge gains and processing costs that fall with prices.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C-58; calculation C-59; calculation C-64

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer financials, ratings or dated bond quotes are supplied (Source readiness records that no quotes were supplied, but the quarterly report prints end-of-period quote-based fair values for the notes, which are used here), so the strong and adequate judgements are made against the issuer's own FY2024 to LTM history and not against comparable producers, and they would move if peers show lower leverage or a cheaper cost position.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The balance-sheet current ratio of 0.74x is below the 1.00x floor in the annual report, but the floor uses the credit agreement's definition, so the liquidity conclusion assumes the stated covenant compliance holds and cannot test it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Hedge volumes are printed per day in Mmbtu and production in mcf, and the annual report labels its benchmark gas price per mcf in one table and per Mmbtu in another with no conversion stated, so the hedge coverage percentages are approximate and could change the cash flow stability conclusion by a few points only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 149; calculation C-31; calculation C-32; calculation C-33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Reserve present values and volumes are management estimates at regulatory prices, before income taxes and without derivatives, so the asset coverage multiples support the loss-severity view only as a rough indicator and no recovery ranking by instrument is drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first strength is low leverage with high cover: total debt of USD 780.92 million against LTM EBITDA of USD 1,593.77 million gives 0.49x and cash interest cover of 20.33x, which leaves room to absorb a price fall, repay the revolver and keep the 2030 maturities refinanceable. The second is a long, undrawn funding runway: USD 1,540.90 million is undrawn on a revolver that matures in 2030, and the borrowing base of USD 3,000.00 million is above the commitments, so liquidity does not depend on market access. The third is a deep, low-reinvestment-risk asset base, with reserve life of 22.23 years and 71% of proved reserves developed, so cash flow can be sustained within the capital budget and the reserve present value of USD 11,566 million at FY2025 is 9.50x principal. The fourth is discretionary capital spending and creditor-aligned distributions: LTM free cash flow of USD 727.19 million is 0.46x EBITDA, 9M 2026 shareholder returns were 28.24% of free cash flow, and there is no sponsor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 8–9, 34; 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-03; calculation C-07; calculation C-11; calculation C-14; calculation C-53; calculation C-42; calculation C-71

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is single-basin gas price exposure: substantially all output comes from the Marcellus Shale, 64% of proved reserves are natural gas, and gas derivatives cover only 20.59% of Q3 2026 production for 2027, so a gas price fall reaches cash flow quickly. The second is fixed transport and processing cost: minimum commitments of USD 5,857.88 million at FY2025 rose by about USD 1,500 million in 9M 2026, and each year's minimum is at least 10.28x LTM cash interest, so margins fall faster than revenue. The third is dependence on the bank facility with almost no cash, so a borrowing base cut or a covenant problem would reach liquidity directly, while covenant headroom cannot be calculated. The fourth is the open merger: control of the capital structure would pass to a group in which Range holders would own about 27%, and creditor treatment, the revolver and the notes' repurchase right are not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 92; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 9–11, 17–19, 38; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-32; calculation C-35; calculation C-36

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Range is an independent producer of natural gas, NGLs and oil that operates almost all of its production from the Marcellus Shale in Pennsylvania as one operating segment, with a holding company whose subsidiaries guarantee the revolver and the notes. Proved reserves equal 22.23 years of FY2025 production, so reinvestment risk is low and the asset base can support debt over the maturity horizon, but production, pipeline access and political and regulatory exposure sit in one basin. Revenue is market-priced: in 9M 2026 natural gas was 57.78%, NGLs 36.45% and oil 5.78% of product sales, so credit quality follows Appalachian gas and NGL prices more than oil. The business therefore generates durable volume but not durable price, which supports debt service capacity and refinancing confidence at current prices and offers little revenue visibility beyond the hedged portion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 12, 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 19, 23; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C-71; calculation C-30

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership does not weaken creditor protection today, but the merger could change it. Range is a listed company with no sponsor or controlling shareholder identified in the documents supplied, so sponsor extraction and fund-life pressure are not in play; ownership percentages and the full board are in a proxy statement that was not supplied. The subsidiary guarantees are full and joint, with release on a sale of the guarantor or its designation as an unrestricted subsidiary, so the guarantor perimeter can shrink without creditor consent. The merger signed on 2026-10-25 would give EQT shareholders about 73% and Range shareholders about 27% of the combined company at a fixed exchange ratio, which moves financial policy and distributions to a larger group whose creditor terms are not described. Observed behaviour is creditor-aligned, with notes repaid at maturity, repurchased below par in 2024 and 2025 and called at a small premium in January 2026, but governance and creditor alignment after closing are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is cyclical, price-taking and not contractually recurring, so it is unpredictable beyond the hedged portion. Range sells at index-based prices to utilities, marketers, midstream companies and industrial users and has no pricing power; in 9M 2026 realized prices before settlements rose 11.95% and production rose 5.74%, but in Q3 2026 the average NYMEX gas price fell 3.91% year on year and the realized gas price fell 7.03%, which management attributes to US production growth and uncertain winter demand. Management expects LNG export growth and power demand to keep longer-term gas prices constructive, which is a view and not a contract; the credit consequence is that revenue durability depends on a market the issuer cannot influence, with hedges smoothing only part of the next two years.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21, 24; calculation C-26; calculation C-25; calculation C-27; calculation C-28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended against moderate volume or price pressure but not against a deep fall, because the largest cost is fixed. Transport, gathering, processing and compression is 54.86% of costs, rests on minimum commitments, and per-unit cost rose to USD 1.55 per mcfe; direct operating and general and administrative costs are small per unit and rose on workovers, water hauling and employee costs. The LTM EBITDA margin of 45.14% was 30.11% at FY2024, so operating leverage cuts both ways: the recovery in prices lifted the margin by 15.03 percentage points, and a fall of similar size would remove it. Processing charges that are a percentage of proceeds fall with prices, which is the main automatic cost relief, and tariff changes on intrastate pipelines could raise fixed charges. The credit consequence is that cash flow available for debt service falls faster than revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 57, 108; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 21–22, 28; calculation C-34; calculation C-19; calculation C-20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA converts durably to free cash flow at current prices, and the conversion is helped by low cash taxes and flexible capital spending. LTM free cash flow of USD 727.19 million was 0.46x EBITDA after capital expenditure of USD 692.07 million, which is 48.76% of operating cash flow and mostly development of the existing position, with no maintenance and growth split disclosed. Cash interest was small at 4.92% of LTM EBITDA, and cash taxes of USD 11.08 million in 9M 2026 reflect federal net operating losses that will be used up, so cash taxes and the alternative minimum tax become a headwind. Working capital absorbed USD 46.40 million in 9M 2026, which is small against operating cash flow. Capital spending is discretionary within the year, so it is the first lever in a downturn and supports free cash flow ahead of the 2030 maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 93, 127; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rrc.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 16, 33; calculation C-14; calculation C-15; calculation C-13; calculation C-17; calculation C-39

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense but works through costs and acreage rather than customers, so the credit effect is on margin durability. The annual report describes substantial competition from larger companies with greater financial resources for leases, services, personnel and pipeline capacity, and says there is little long-term price advantage for a commodity producer; this means Range's margin relies on cost position and balance-sheet strength, which low leverage supports. New entrants matter less than supply response by existing producers: management attributes the lower Q3 2026 gas price to US production growth, which pressures realized prices and the borrowing base value of reserves. Substitutes such as wind, solar and nuclear are cited as a risk if technology and policy support grow, but management expects power demand and LNG exports to support gas demand, so the substitution threat is a long-dated pressure on gas demand and refinancing appetite. Buyers have limited power because alternative purchasers are readily available and Range sells at index prices to many users, so buyer risk is price, not volume or credit. Suppliers hold the most power: third-party pipelines and processors set capacity and fees under long minimum commitments, and capacity constraints can lead to shut-ins, which is the channel from supplier power to cash flow and liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Policy and economic factors are material to credit quality; social and technology factors are not primary drivers on the supplied evidence. The methane waste emissions charge was postponed until 2034 by legislation and the regulator extended some compliance deadlines, which lowers near-term compliance cost but leaves a possible later cost; the federal administration has restarted reviews of LNG export projects, which supports demand for Appalachian gas. Changes in intrastate pipeline rate design could raise fixed transport charges and reduce netbacks, and tariffs on imported goods can raise service costs; the economic exposure is commodity price volatility, inflation in diesel and services, and the floating rate on the revolver, where a rise of 1 percentage point costs USD 2.94 million a year. The credit consequence is that policy risk is mostly about the timing of demand and cost, not about solvency, while price volatility is the dominant economic risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Credit strengths are the low leverage of 0.49x, the undrawn revolver of USD 1,540.90 million, long reserve life, hedges over part of the next three years and creditor-aligned distributions. Credit weaknesses are single-basin gas price exposure, fixed transport commitments, cash of USD 12 thousand so that liquidity is only the revolver, and unknown covenant headroom. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are structural LNG export and power demand for gas, which would support prices, and the merger if the documents show Range's debt assumed or guaranteed by a stronger obligor. Threats that could weaken it are a gas price fall like that of FY2024, a borrowing base cut after a price decline, rising cash taxes as net operating losses are used, a merger that leaves creditors behind more debt, and a debt-funded buyback with USD 1,421.65 million of authorization remaining.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial profile is strong and improving on leverage, cover and liquidity, average on cash flow stability because it follows gas prices, and unestablished on covenant headroom and market access. Supports are low leverage of 0.49x, cover of 20.33x, USD 1,540.90 million of undrawn revolver and LTM free cash flow of USD 727.19 million. Constraints are the fixed transport claim, the single facility and the merger. The trend since FY2024 is a fall in leverage from 2.33x to 0.49x as prices recovered and debt was repaid, so it is partly cyclical. Missing data points are the credit agreement and its covenant definitions, ratings, peer comparisons, the merger documents and any filing after 2026-10-27.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The next 12 to 24 months look supportive for cash flow and uncertain for control. Management plans a 2026 capital budget of USD 650 million to USD 700 million for modest production growth, with the program funded from operating cash flow, and has hedged more than 30% of the rest of 2026; the merger is expected to close in Q1 2027, after which financial policy and the capital structure are not described in the filings. Headwinds are the Q3 2026 gas price fall, rising cash taxes, higher fixed transport minimums and the next annual borrowing base redetermination, which could reduce availability if reserve values fall. Over three to five years, tailwinds are expected LNG export and power demand growth and a long reserve life; headwinds are that the revolver and the notes both mature in 2030, requiring refinancing, that proved undeveloped reserves need a large development spend, and that the transport commitments run for up to 15 years. These support or pressure revenue durability, margins and liquidity as described above; they do not change the stand-alone view without the merger terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside is a return of low Appalachian gas prices of the kind seen in FY2024, when the NYMEX benchmark used for reserves was 37.17% lower than in 2025, while minimum transport payments stay due. As an illustration, sized to return EBITDA to the FY2024 level of USD 727.72 million and not as a forecast, a fall of 27.10% in realized prices on LTM product sales removes USD 866.05 million of EBITDA. Revenue falls by the same amount, the EBITDA margin falls to 27.31%, and operating cash flow falls to USD 553.21 million, so free cash flow before dividends becomes a deficit of USD 138.86 million at current capital expenditure and a deficit of USD 230.94 million after LTM dividends of USD 92.08 million. Total debt over EBITDA rises to 1.07x, or 1.59x including claims outside debt, and EBITDA still covers cash interest 9.28x. Funding one year of that cash gap on the revolver lifts total debt to USD 1,011.86 million and 1.39x EBITDA and leaves USD 1,309.96 million undrawn. Management's levers are capital spending, where a cut of 20.06% closes the gap before dividends, then buybacks and the dividend, and hedge gains and lower processing charges would add relief that the illustration omits. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, because the first debt maturity is in 2030 and USD 1,309.96 million of the revolver would remain undrawn after that year; the exposures are a borrowing base cut at redetermination and the first break in cash flow, which is the fixed transport cost. The observable triggers are quarterly product sales below the prior-year quarter, a falling margin, a rising revolver balance and any reduction of the borrowing base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Range presents an adequate business profile supported by a long reserve life, an operated Marcellus position and hedges over part of the next three years, but credit quality is constrained by single-basin gas price exposure, fixed transport commitments of USD 5,857.88 million and a single bank facility. Cash-flow durability appears adequate at current prices, with USD 727.19 million of LTM free cash flow, and weaker if gas prices return to FY2024 levels. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on holding leverage low, keeping the borrowing base above the commitments and the terms of the merger, since the revolver and the notes both mature in 2030. The primary downside path is a gas price fall that meets fixed transport payments and a borrowing base cut. Further analysis would require the credit agreement, the indenture, the merger documents, ratings and peer data. Top risk: a gas price fall combined with fixed transport commitments and an unstated treatment of creditors in the merger.
